items.title: ELDEN RING Movie Wraps Filming, but We’re Still Waiting Nearly Two More Years to See It
items.summary: Production has officially wrapped on A24
items.content:
Production has officially wrapped on A24's Elden Ring , which means the cameras have stopped rolling on one of the most ambitious video game adaptations ever attempted. Now, fans have nearly two years to wait before they can finally experience the Lands Between on the big screen.

That's a long wait, but this isn't the kind of movie anyone wants rushed. Between adapting FromSoftware's sprawling fantasy world, bringing its unforgettable monsters and magic to life, and translating its famously cryptic storytelling into a feature film, there's a lot riding on what happens next. Fortunately, it sounds like the filmmakers have given themselves the time they need to get it right.

A24 is a studio known for prestige filmmaking rather than giant fantasy epics, so it will be interesting to see how this movie turns out. A lot of people are watching this production closely.

Principal photography officially wrapped on July 30, and A24 confirmed that Elden Ring remains set for a theatrical release on March 3, 2028. The studio also reminded fans that the movie is being shot specifically for IMAX, suggesting this adaptation is aiming to deliver an experience that feels every bit as massive as the game that inspired it.

For anyone outside the gaming world, two years of post prodction might sound like an incredibly long stretch between filming and release. But Elden Ring fans don't seem bothered by it at all.

Across social media, the reaction has been surprisingly positive, with many players expressing that they'd much rather see the filmmakers take their time than rush an adaptation of one of gaming's most ambitious fantasy worlds.

That mindset makes perfect sense. The movie will eventually have to win over audiences who have never stepped foot in the Lands Between, but right now the people paying the closest attention are the fans who've already spent hundreds of hours exploring every hidden dungeon, battling impossible bosses, and piecing together the game's mysterious lore.

Gamers are also used to waiting. Major game releases often take four or five years between installments, so a lengthy post-production schedule doesn't feel unusual.

Then there's the technical side of the challenge. The Lands Between isn't a world you can simply build on a soundstage. It's packed with towering monsters, surreal landscapes, bizarre creatures, and magical imagery that simply can't exist without extensive visual effects.

If the filmmakers want this world to capture the same atmosphere that made the game unforgettable, the VFX team needs time to bring those environments and creatures to life in a believable way. Rushing that process could undermine everything that makes Elden Ring so visually distinctive.

Visual effects are only part of the equation, though. FromSoftware built Elden Ring around fragmented storytelling, cryptic dialogue, item descriptions, and lore that players slowly assemble themselves.

Turning that experience into a traditional feature film presents another major creative hurdle. Garland has to figure out how much mystery to preserve while still crafting a story that audiences unfamiliar with the game can follow.

That's a balancing act that can't be solved overnight, and an extended post-production schedule gives the filmmakers more opportunities to refine the edit until it feels right.

Considering the enormous scope of the adaptation and the expectations surrounding it, taking the extra time feels less like a delay and more like the smartest path forward. If this movie is going to capture the scale, mystery, and unforgettable atmosphere of Elden Ring, it's worth letting the team finish crafting it without racing the clock.

The dark fantasy title has already passed 43,000 concurrent players on Steam since launching July 29. News By GBest - Aug 04, 2026 05:08 AM EST Filed Under: Action A new multiplayer title has carved out an early audience on Steam by combining two popular formulas. Mistfall Hunter , developed by Bellring Games and published with Skystone Games , mixes skill-based Soulslike combat with extraction-style PvPvE gameplay and wraps the result in a dark fantasy presentation that draws clear visual inspiration from Elden Ring .

The game launched on July 29 across Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S , and is also available through Xbox Game Pass . In a short time it has recorded a peak of 43,741 concurrent players on Steam, with numbers still climbing. Across all platforms the developer reports more than 500,000 players so far. A 10 percent launch discount remains active on Steam until August 12, bringing the current price to $22.49 .

Mistfall Hunter sits in the extraction genre but rejects the usual modern military or sci-fi framing. Players drop into dark fantasy environments, scavenge for resources and gear, fight both monsters and other players, and attempt to extract with their spoils. Matches support solo play or squads of up to three. The loop will feel familiar to anyone who has spent time with ARC Raiders or similar extraction shooters, yet the execution leans heavily on melee-focused, stamina-managed, position-critical combat associated with Soulslike design.

Six distinct classes form the foundation of character progression. Each comes with a deep talent tree that allows meaningful specialization. The combat system uses free aim and rewards careful spacing, timing, and resource management rather than pure statistical overwhelming force. On Steam the game carries the Soulslike user tag, reflecting how closely its melee exchanges track with the genre’s expectations even while the overall structure remains extraction-based.

Visually the game commits to a gloomy, high-fantasy aesthetic. Environments, enemy design, and overall tone frequently invite comparisons to Elden Ring , though the multiplayer extraction framework keeps the experience distinct. The combination has proven effective at standing out in a crowded marketplace where pure Soulslikes and pure extraction games are both common.

Player reviews currently sit at "Mostly Positive." Feedback frequently highlights the novelty of the genre mix, the quality of the visuals, and the satisfaction of the combat. Common criticisms focus on server performance issues, uneven class balance, and a limited number of maps that can make repeated runs feel repetitive. Because the core loop is landing with players, these problems are the kind that ongoing updates can address.

The absence of pay-to-win mechanics has also been noted positively. Progression and power come from gameplay and seasonal advancement rather than cash purchases that affect balance. Seasons provide a structure for ongoing content and resets, a standard expectation in the extraction space that helps maintain long-term engagement.

Smaller-scale projects often have more freedom to test unusual combinations than large-budget productions. Mistfall Hunter takes the risk of marrying two audiences that do not always overlap: players who want the methodical, high-stakes feel of Soulslike combat and those who enjoy the tension of extracting under pressure from both AI and human opponents. Early numbers suggest enough players are interested in that intersection to give the game a viable starting audience.

The limited map pool remains the most immediate content concern. Extraction games rely on environmental knowledge and varied routes to stay fresh. A small selection of maps can accelerate the point at which runs begin to feel predictable. How quickly Bellring Games expands the available locations will likely influence whether the current player base continues to grow or begins to taper off after the initial wave of curiosity.

Server stability and class tuning are more straightforward technical and design tasks. Both are typical post-launch priorities for multiplayer games that launch into an already active concurrent audience. The fact that the game has reached more than 40,000 concurrent users while still carrying these issues indicates that the underlying concept is carrying a good deal of the momentum.

Mistfall Hunter is available now on Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. Game Pass subscribers can access it as part of the service. The current Steam discount makes this an inexpensive entry point for players curious about a dark fantasy take on extraction gameplay that puts deliberate, Soulslike combat at the center of every encounter. Whether the game can sustain its early numbers will depend on how effectively the team responds to the map, balance, and infrastructure feedback already appearing in reviews. For the moment, it has succeeded in turning a hybrid concept into a visible new release on Steam.

items.title: Elden Ring DLC rumours abuzz following FromSoftware's cryptic social media activity
items.content:
It's been two long years since Elden Ring's last expansion, and players refuse to believe that FromSoftware is done with the wildly captivating fantasy realm it created.

Although the base game is entering its Bloodborne and Skyrim arc, being a legacy RPG that continues to surprise fans with secrets only now being uncovered , Elden Ring has a lot more to give.

Yet it has been two years since Shadow of the Erdtree was dropped as the ultimate 'send-off', described in our review as "a fitting conclusion to FromSoftware’s biggest, and most successful title to date."

Despite FromSoftware cooking up the online multiplayer spin-off Nightreign in May last year, and the clear 'ending' that the Shadow of the Erdtree brought, fans of the fantasy realm still want more from this award-winning title.

Now, activity on the developers' social media page has sent the community into a frenzy, with many people claiming that a new Elden Ring DLC could be on the way.

Hot on the back of Elden Ring's success, FromSoftware has been devoted to bringing players the 'next' Bloodborne , with The Duskbloods landing on Nintendo Switch 2 as the developers' ambitious spiritual successor.

Yet it's clear that there is still love for Elden Ring , as new posts on X (previously Twitter) showcased some new content that players are now convinced ties directly into a Godwyn DLC.

The inconspicuous post appeared to be harmless at first watch, but the 12-second video has now amassed over 6.5 million views, as those fans who have been waiting for years for more content have come to some interesting conclusions.

All the video shows is a quick pony ride through the Siofra River, as a lack of giant crab and Ancestral Follower enemies made for a 'quiet wonder'.

But it is a different type of post from what we usually see the developers release, and highlights new skins for Torrent that are quickly being construed as a hype-building device for a new expansion.

Read Next: 7 Essential Elden Ring Mods Which Offer A Brand New Challenge

Spinning social media into a mass craze, players are fuelled on copium.

"FROMSOFT RELEASE GODWYN DLC AND MY LIFE IS YOURS," reads the top comment on the post.

A second said, "HUNT for the DEMIGODS > shows empty Siofra River > one way to get to Deeproot Depths is through the Siofra Aqueduct and transporter coffin > GODWYN DLC ?????"

items.title: The action game I’ve been obsessed with for 3 years is now on Nintendo Switch 2 — and it’ll keep you busy until Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition
items.summary: Lies of P is instantly one of the Switch 2’s best games
items.content:
Lies of P is instantly one of the Switch 2’s best games

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Neowiz / Round8 Studio) Copy link Facebook X Reddit Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter It’s no exaggeration to say that I’ve been obsessed with Lies of P since I first played it at launch back in September 2023. This action-Soulslike was my personal favorite game of that year (despite extraordinarily strong competition). So, when the Nintendo Switch 2 arrived last summer, I was desperately hoping Lies of P would head over to the hybrid console ASAP.

Fortunately, I didn’t have to wait very long. Just over 12 months after the Switch 2’s launch, and nearly three years after its initial release, Lies of P: Complete Edition comes to Nintendo’s platform this week (on Thursday, August 6). I’ve had the chance to check it out early, and it’s pretty much exactly what I hoped: The same great Lies of P game, now on Switch 2.

Its release timing feels particularly appropriate, as Lies of P launches on Switch 2 just a few weeks ahead of the hotly anticipated Elden Ring : Tarnish Edition. So, if you need a game to hold you over until revisiting FromSoftware’s behemoth, this excellent Soulslike is the perfect title for the occasion. It remains a must-play for fans of challenging action-RPGs.

The award-winning Lies of P experience comes to Switch 2 in this Complete Edition that includes the full base and the Overture DLC expansion. In this Soulslike, you play a powerful puppet, exploring the fallen city of Krat after a devastating event has left the gothic metropolis in ruins. Unravel a dark story, defeat intimidating bosses, and craft a character that fits your specific playstyle.

In short, Lies of P takes clear clues from the Dark Souls series, created by FromSoftware, the developer of Elden Ring. It’s a demanding action-RPG that emphasizes challenging combat encounters, build-crafting, and memorable boss battles that might take you dozens of attempts.

Loosely based on Carlo Collodi’s “The Adventures of Pinocchio,” you play a living puppet, referred to as P, who must venture through the gothic city of Krat in the aftermath of an event known as the “Puppet Frenzy,” in which the once servient puppets turned on their human masters.

I just played Final Fantasy VII Rebirth on Switch 2 — here's how it compares to PS5 Pro Forget Nintendo — it’s Capcom keeping the Switch 2 alive right now Finally got a Switch 2? These are my 12 must-play Nintendo-exclusive games It’s an intriguing setup, and Lies of P does a great job offering players small snippets of story, rewarding curiosity and a willingness to piece together the overarching narrative via optional collectibles. But as much as I enjoy the rich lore of Lies of P, it’s the punishing combat that shines brightest.

Lies of P might be part of the “Soulslike” genre (named for the aforementioned Dark Souls), but its closest comparison is actually FromSoftware’s 2015 PS4 exclusive Bloodborne . Combat encounters are fast and fluid, with the best strategy revolving around relentless pressure and, if you can nail the timing, making use of parries to stun enemies.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The game also packs some of the most well-designed boss encounters of any Soulslike. You’ll square off against all manner of towering foes, from an electrified police robot to a mutated Archbishop spewing blue goo. I don’t want to veer into spoilers, but several of Lies of P’s best bosses rival even the works of genre originator FromSoftware. And the final boss is a doozy.

Even if wholly new ideas are thin on the ground — though the game's weapon combining system is unique — Lies of P mixes the best elements of its Souls inspirations to deliver a consistently satisfying action experience. Each victory is hard-earned, and levels beg to be explored.

The game also has several built-in guardrails to help you pick your level of challenge. There are multiple difficulty settings (originally added post-launch, but available on Switch 2 from day one), and the majority of bosses allow you to summon a helpful NPC companion, which makes things considerably easier. Lies of P doesn't have to be brutally tough, if you wish.

items.title: The Soulslike genre has grown stale after Elden Ring, and only FromSoftware can take it to strange new places
items.summary: The Soulslike genre is in a generally healthy spot, but we're at the whims of Miyazaki if we want true innovation.
items.content:
Image credit: FromSoftware Feature by Ed Thorn Former Reviews Editor Published on Aug. 3, 2026, 12:59 p.m. 65 comments Follow Dark Souls Sometimes I have to remind myself that I’m a cliché, a person first compelled to write about games because I slew Dark Souls ’ Gwynn, Lord Of Cinder and sat quietly for a moment before thinking to myself, “Hit me, come on, hit me!”. No, I was not okay. But my understanding of games shifted in that tiny university room: they could be overcome, not just completed. FromSoftware’s dark fantasy lands, with their puzzle-box intricacy and dribbly residents, ushered in the "Soulslike" as other developers sought to cash in on masochists like me.

Here I am, still a masochist, still someone who adores a Souls and/or ‘like, but who stares at the offerings nowadays and thinks, "Please, someone hit me". These games have stagnated, to the point where it feels like we’re all waiting for FromSoftware to emerge from the fog and beat our asses in a way we’ve not quite seen before.

To sum up a Soulslike for you, it’s not necessarily a 1:1 attempt at cloning Demon’s Souls or its later Dark Souls compatriots. It’s an inspiration or interpretation of its cursed DNA, like how in the fragrance community you might have, say, Louis Vuitton’s Imagination: a £300 bottle of juice that smells a bit like an expensive bar of soap. Other fragrance houses notice its popularity and complexity, then churn out ‘dupes’ inspired by the signature smelly. Some step away from Imagination’s citrus and dial up the soap. Some dial down the tea note. Others add a spritz of bug spray into the mix. The best dupes take the original formula and produce some juice that elevates certain elements, even if they’re working with less expensive ingredients.

It’s no secret that Souls games contain facets of other popular games that came before them. Third-person combat, dodge-rolling, checkpoints, punishing combat, a throaty witch who bookends her sentences with croaks of "He he he". I’d say the things that make a Soulslike distinct, the notes if you will, are its tug of war with tension. As you slay baddies, you’ll collect Souls that you can spend to level up at bonfires, except that: 1) If you die, you’ll lose all of your moolah and have only one chance to scoop it back up; 2) Bonfires act as checkpoints, except they’ll vary in how generously they’ll pop up.

I’d also argue that a playful map completes the trifecta of a Soulslike. Pretty much all of the signature Souls games see you unpick maps that bury secrets in labyrinthine caverns, or whirl you skywards until you arrive at a cliff edge, look across the ruined landscape, and realise you’ve come oh-so-very far. It’s probably the closest you’ll ever get to a pat on the back or a light jostle of "Well done pal" from FromSoftware.

So as Souls become more popular, how did the first likers emerge? Team Ninja’s Nioh is a prime example of a dev house applying their own strengths to the formula while reducing the potency of others. Out went the knotty world, replaced by missions and a map. Out went cackling witches and subtle environmental storytelling, replaced by crystals and cringe. Out went fairly simple menus, in went crashing waves of loot lapping at your tabis and bioluminescent shores swimming with stats. Crucially, out went dodge rolling and average sword swings, and in went Team Ninja’s signature approach to scraps that made FromSoft’s fluidity seem languid by comparison. Demons are ingredients, to be minced through dizzying fighting game combos and a Ki (stamina) bar you can Active Reload like a prime "Eat shit and die" Marcus Fenix.

Others followed, like The Surge and Mortal Shell and Lords Of The Fallen (2014) and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty . All of them scrabbling for that singular gimmick, like robotic limbs and hardening carapaces and knocking over lads with shields. Somewhere in-between them all, FromSoftware added Dark Souls 2 , 3 , Bloodborne and Sekiro , in what I’d consider an era where iteration from the OGs lay in fine readjustments, thematic excellence, rhythmic groove and a foray into extra-curricular dungeon crawling.

Then, like a Patches kick to the nuts, FromSoftware dropped Elden Ring in 2022. Arguably the biggest reinvention of the Souls genre in years, they’d stretched their smaller puzzle boxes of yore outwards like fresh pizza dough, topped it with a frightening array of locations and stuffed the crusts with murderous goblins. Sites of Grace replaced bonfires, whose glistening trails would point in the direction you’re meant to go, so you’d naturally seek the opposite trail in search of hot honey and pepperoni.

Arguably, though, Elden Ring was FromSoftware pushing Souls further into the mainstream in what felt like a natural, if predictable, evolution of the formula. 'Open world' is an easy sell on the store page, and entices a huge new market of non-Soulsers who respond to scope and scale and bombast if presented to them through a simpler lens. Not that Dark Souls didn’t have all of these things - Elden Ring, of course, upped the anté - but it just didn’t feel quite as beholden to revenue targets.

Since then we’ve had the stellar Black Myth: Wukong , a blockbuster open-world-ish adventure where a monkey with a staff clatters his way through gods. Team Ninja shrugged Nioh 3 into a superb open-world blend. Dark-fantasy-Pinnochio-like Lies Of P was an outlier in the sense it felt like a Soulslike from the previous generation of Soulslikes, although it did toy around with 'Lying' to wiggle the narrative around (meh) and switching out your robotic limbs (pretty cool).

Delve into Steam Next Fest, or just Steam in general, and you’ll find a plethora of Soulslikes that largely take one gimmick and run with it. Look at The Lords Of The Fallen (2023), which introduced a cool interdimensional death lamp but largely played like any other Soulser. Look at Thymesia , with its zippy combat and - you get it.

FromSoft are now shifting their frozen needle towards multiplayer antics, given their co-op roguelike Elden Ring: Nightreign launched not too long ago and their upcoming Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods isn’t far off. What will it have to offer? All we know as I’m writing this is that it’s a PvPvE deal, very probably their take on the extraction shooter boom, with a fairly self-evident hope that it’ll print money like those battle royales once did. What I’m trying to say, with some sadness, is that Duskbloods looks like a symptom of the game industry more than a game I’m interested in.

Have Soulslikes, then, reached Smartphone Mountain? Where the peak is Sen's Fortress and the next frontier is another fortress that folds outwards? Yes, for now. Mistfall Hunter is another PvPvE special that’s due out soon, and although James has been liking FPSoulslike Valor Mortis it still feels like most developers are chasing industry trends, while the rest of us sit hoping that Miyazaki's off feeding some singleplayer monstrosity that'll break containment soon.

None of this is to say Soulslikes are on the way out, or that their cadence of sameyness is entirely a bad thing, I just think the best chance of true innovation lies in a creative twist courtesy of the original creators. Honestly, I hope FromSoft shift away from the expansiveness of Elden Ring, shrink things down and instead push its ghostfriend-conjuring summon systems further and deeper. Take cues from JRPGs, perhaps, where we're commanding a small party for the first time, or toy around with bonfires as less of a resting spot and more of a fleeting chance to commune with other players in an otherworldly marketplace.

items.title: Pre-orders for the Nintendo Switch 2 'Elden Ring Tarnished Edition' package begin Wednesday, August 5!
items.summary: Source: Bandai Namco EntertainmentBandai Namco Entertainment Korea (Branch Manager Jang Tae-geun) announced that pre-orders for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 package of 'Elden Ring...
items.content:
Bandai Namco Entertainment Korea (Branch Manager Jang Tae-geun) announced that pre-orders for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 package of 'Elden Ring Tarnished Edition' will begin on Wednesday, August 5.

'Elden Ring Tarnished Edition' includes the base 'Elden Ring' game and the major downloadable content 'Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree,' released in June 2024. It also features various additional elements, such as new armor and equipment for the spectral steed, Torrent.

In the Nintendo Switch™ 2 version of 'Elden Ring Tarnished Edition,' players can explore vast fields and dungeons, discover unknown worlds, and experience the sense of accomplishment that comes from overcoming challenges and obstacles. Players will forge their own path through the vast, seamless world of the Lands Between.

'Elden Ring' was released in 2022 under the direction of FromSoftware director and creator of the DARK SOULS® series, Hidetaka Miyazaki, and is based on a mythic story crafted by George R. R. Martin, author of the bestselling fantasy series 'A Song of Ice and Fire.'

Players can explore vast fields and dungeons, discover unknown worlds, and enjoy the sense of accomplishment that comes from overcoming challenges and obstacles. This action RPG, set in an authentic dark fantasy world, has surpassed 30 million units in cumulative sales worldwide to date.

More detailed information about the game can be found on the Bandai Namco Entertainment Korea official website.

items.title: Elden Ring Fans Believe FromSoftware's Mysterious Post is a Teaser for a New DLC
items.content:
0 03 Aug 02:44 Recently, FromSoftware studio intrigued Elden Ring fans. The developers published a short video on social media.

The 12-second gameplay footage shows a character riding through a location – the Siofra River. The video was captioned with a phrase that can be translated as: "Even in the perilous hunt for demigods, there are moments of quiet admiration." In a few days, it garnered almost 7 million views and numerous comments.

Many fans saw this publication by the developers as a hint for another Elden Ring DLC. For example, they could imagine content related to Godwyn the Golden – according to the lore, he is the son of Queen Marika the Eternal. This character is the first demigod to die.

1 / 2 FromSoftware, Inc., Bandai Namco Entertainment Also, some community members took the opportunity to urge FromSoftware to return to Elden Ring Nightreign – the game has not received any DLCs or updates for a long time.

Currently, FromSoftware is working on The Duskbloods for the Nintendo Switch 2 console. The developers plan to conduct network testing of the game from August 21 to 23.

items.title: I'm Just Not Into Souls Games, I'm Being Tested Enough As It Is
items.summary: I am taking the opportunity this week to get something off my chest, something I haven’t been able (or willing) to share so publicly before: I hate Souls games. All of them. Even the ones that don’t have Souls in their name, because they still count. 🤝This is
items.content:
I am taking the opportunity this week to get something off my chest, something I haven’t been able (or willing) to share so publicly before: I hate Souls games. All of them. Even the ones that don’t have Souls in their name, because they still count.

Whether it’s Demon’s Souls or its sequel, Sekiro or Bloodborne or Elden Ring , if there’s enough Miyazaki and unforgiving combat in it to warrant being called a Souls Game, get it out of my face. I don’t want anything to do with it. I would rather punch myself unconscious than subject myself to its trials.

I understand this can be a sacrilegious thing to say as a games writer. It is generally held that these games are beloved by all, respected by consumer and critic alike, some of the all-time greats of the medium. I literally cannot think of anyone else I have been able to share my disdain with in professional (or even personal!) circles; everyone else is always “oh this boss was so hard” this and “I died 117 times before getting past this bit, it was AMAZING” that.

I am a middle-aged man whose life currently consists of a succession of ordeals. I have seen my career blown up twice through no fault of my own . I am trying to pay off a mortgage with declining income amid an inflationary crisis. To do this, I am working three jobs, one of which involves begging strangers for money on a weekly basis, and which for three 16-hour days of the week I have to fit around another job. I have two teenage kids.

The very last thing I want to do when I sit down at the end of a very long day is to suffer more trials. I do not want to have to act fast, to memorise patterns, to beat my head against a boss 99 times in the pursuit of fun. I need my personal time to relax , and these games are the opposite of relaxing! And I certainly don’t feel the need to prove anything to myself by beating a "hard" video game either, I am not 12 years old, I know where my strengths (and weaknesses!) are by now, both in gaming and as a person. I can see the appeal there for others, and will never try to tell you not to enjoy these games, but for me and my needs and my tastes, the premise of a game built around repeated failure and precise timing is torture.

I find this really interesting, though, because as someone who has played hundreds of video games over the last 20 years I can’t think of another major series where I am even remotely as repulsed as I am by Souls games. I love Yakuza , and it’s got the same menu obsession and (in older titles at least) a more forgiving version of its punishing melee combat. I’ve always found something to get me through a AAA shooter , I like driving cars, I’ve played too many FIFA games and even in the handful of Nintendo franchises I’ve bounced off ( Metroid ) there’s something to admire. I have even, gasp, found space in my heart to fall in love with a Hideo Kojima game . Fast or slow, easy or hard, I have loved games (or found something to love within them) across the genre and difficulty spectrum.

But Souls games? It’s like they’re precision-engineered to bounce right off me, in every way humanly possible. I hate everything , from the art design (yuck) to the combat to the relentless concentration required to do anything to the way that so many people are so slavishly in love with something I detest, a big “we love Souls ” club that seems to include everyone I know except me and…

Ah. As I lean further back into the therapist’s couch I've conjured in my mind while writing this, maybe there's something in that. A lot of the games I truly love, the ones with little guys and taking turns , are often relatively niche pursuits, never getting anywhere near the kind of popular critical mass Souls games enjoy, something everyone I know can talk about online or at a party. Maybe I don’t just hate the game, I hate the players as well, because everyone always seems to be having so much fun beating things and talking to friends about it and falling in love with a very particular kind of game and I’m left out because I just don’t feel the same way. Bah humbug, etc, and all that entails.

Oh well! Fuck it. I still don’t like the games, I’m never going to pretend I do just so I can be part of some online discourse. If that means living the rest of my days as a Souls hater, forever on the outside looking in (on the internet), then so be it!

It's Hater Week here on Aftermath . This week we’re letting the hate flow through us by examining what it means to be a hater (and… a lover?), venting about some of our biggest pet peeves in games and life, and giving others a space to do the same.

items.title: What it's like beating Elden Ring twice a week for 4 years: "I think it's the greatest game that's ever been made"
items.content:
Playing FromSoftware's best RPG for a living takes you to some weird places

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Bandai Namco) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter FromSoftware is in a curious position. It released Elden Ring, its most successful and arguably best game, and ever since has exclusively released games that are very different to Elden Ring. And yes, that does include Elden Ring Nightreign, an experimental spinoff that cleverly reuses some assets and shrinks the world, then builds a PvE battle royale experience around it.

We've had Armored Core 6 and we've got The Duskbloods coming, but FromSoftware hasn't announced a new single-player dark fantasy RPG of the kind it's known for. This has left many fans revisiting the RPGs FromSoft has already released, most especially Elden Ring and its gargantuan world and DLC. It's hard to think of anybody who has gotten more out of Elden Ring than Bushy, a challenge runner who's beaten this famously long and difficult RPG over 400 times by his best estimate.

On Twitch and YouTube , Bushy is known for completing challenge runs in Elden Ring, and occasionally other games, that put restrictions on how he plays. Across hundreds of clears, he's amassed a huge collection of absurd rule sets. You have the classics, like one-hitting bosses, never dying, never getting hit, always getting hit, or kicking enemies to death. Mods, some of them commissioned by Bushy just for this purpose, also allow for stranger runs with teleportation, mismatched areas and enemies, or randomized items. Then we get to the truly specific stuff, like his most recent video: " Elden Ring But I Can Only Use White Items ".

It was this color-specific video series that pushed me to reach out to Bushy. Man , I thought, this guy has done everything . And it's easy to think that Bushy must be running out of ideas or growing sick of the game by now, but he tells me he's every bit as in love with Elden Ring as he has been for the past "3,500 to 4,000" hours of game time.

"I think it's the greatest game that's ever been made," Bushy says. "I always just have a ton of fun with it. If I didn't have that much fun with it, I wouldn't still be trying to come up with new, inventive ways to beat it. Don't get me wrong, part of that is absolutely that it's my job, and there are external forces that are encouraging me to play Elden Ring. But I think it's honestly more of a blessing than it is a curse."

7 years ago, the first Elden Ring trailer changed my life A new Elden Ring world record was set just 2 weeks ago, and I keep rewatching the same part One Bloodborne player has spent 3,500 hours helping people with one of FromSoftware's hardest bosses The release of Elden Ring Nightreign did give Bushy some space to play another game, and the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC was a refreshing injection of new content and items, but he always comes back to the game.

He considers the pessimistic read of his position. "You could look at that in a negative light," he says. "You're playing Elden Ring because you have to, because it's the only thing that makes you money. But that's not really how I look at it. Elden Ring is a game that is big enough, massive enough, deep enough, that has such a breadth of content, that having motivation and a reason to actually play it that much is really quite the blessing. I get to play it a whole lot more than other people do."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Bushy's putting every last grain of Elden Ring under the magnifying glass. Like a speedrunner, he talks about individual bosses as things to "practice". His videos often see him deliberately rotate through spells, weapons, and items in order to explain and engage with multiple parts of the game rather than simply using the first winning option he can find, and his rule sets regularly lead to interesting discoveries about overlooked items and strategies. I'm reminded of MMO players running self-sufficient accounts, whose self-imposed challenges force them to play the game in novel ways.

His favorite challenge runs are those that dramatically change the game and are "higher effort" overall, like the one where he was teleported to a random checkpoint every five minutes. He also played the game with an aggression mod that made every enemy follow and attack him at all times, with basically no way to lose or avoid aggro. It didn't go well.

Now, Bushy can just throw out obscene sentences like this: "I've on average beaten the game probably twice a week since the game came out." This schedule wasn't immovable, but his channel history bears it out. I've learned not to underestimate FromSoftware fans, but I certainly haven't met anyone else who's rolled credits this many times. Additionally, Bushy says, "the longest I've gone not playing Elden Ring since it came out has probably been like three weeks."

Bushy is certainly looking forward to future FromSoftware games, but somehow reckons he's got more than enough Elden Ring challenge run ideas left in the tank. When he started playing the game for a living, building on years of streaming other games, he was "hopeful" after his early challenges got some attention. "I made lots of very bad videos and got more views than I had ever gotten at the time," he recalls. Elden Ring's massive audience was enough to turn the game into a career for him, not unlike how creators like VaatiVidya make a living by interpreting FromSoftware lore.

items.title: Is Elden Ring the best of the Souls series?
items.summary: Is Elden Ring the best Soulslike game ever made? Explore how FromSoftware reinvented the genre with open-world freedom, epic boss fights, and unmatched player choice.
items.content:
For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games.

For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games and inspired players of all ages.

Let’s take a look at how ELDEN RING has elevated and perfected the original Souls series formula and explore if ELDEN RING could be the best of the entire Souls series.

The majority of the games were designed by Hidetaka Miyazaki to give players the experience of exploring dark and majestic fantasy worlds full of danger.

There’s also a strong focus on difficulty, world structure, boss fights, and player builds.

The difficulty of the Souls series stems from their combat design. They emphasize deliberate attack and evasion in response to enemy movement, which tends to be quick, fierce, and punishing for players who find themselves out of position at the wrong moment. Players need to carefully observe and learn their foes’ patterns, then react to exploit certain specific attack openings without leaving themselves open as well.

This type of careful, evasive gameplay mimics the danger and strategy of real hand-to-hand combat and the high stakes keeps the tension and excitement rising in each fight. It’s not as simple as playing out a power fantasy where enemies easily fall to repeated mindless button mashing. For most players, this difficulty means that the feeling of mastering Souls series combat is a rush of pure accomplishment.

In the earlier Souls series games , levels are massive, interconnected linear paths. These paths often have several branching paths that reward exploration and puzzle solving, but are limited in terms of true open field exploration, as it’s necessary to follow a specific set order of levels, usually connected by a hub area where players can regroup, level up and open new paths, to progress throughout the game.

In the best Souls series games , carefully studying the environment and enemy behavior can lead to hidden areas or items, a particular strength of the Dark Souls series, and many players consider level design that rewards careful exploration to be a critical feature of Dark Souls-like games .

Throughout the Souls series , boss battles are powerful climatic moments that put a player’s abilities to the test. In the Dark Souls series , specifically, from the Asylum Demon to Slave Knight Gael , the Dark Souls bosses are encounters that inspire fear, awe, pity, and wonder.

Bosses also act as progression gates that require a certain level of fluency with the game’s combat system before the player can continue to explore. Once a player reaches a boss gate, they must either muster the skill to defeat that boss, or continue to practice and grind on earlier enemies.

Unlike the average enemy that players must face in a limited area not much wider than a typical hallway, bosses are frequently found in massive arenas. Bosses in the Souls series also tend to have enhanced abilities that require the player to adapt to attacks that cover huge areas or have extended reach. This ferocity and enlarged battlefield gives the designers space to create exciting, multi-phase duels that are unforgettably intense.

These boss fights also act as a check on the player’s build. No matter which weapons or elements a player prefers, massive and powerful bosses require adaptation.

Experienced players understand how each type of stat affects their damage output and they use all of the gear at their disposal to create a move set that fits their style and is powerful enough to take down bosses.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
